title: This Soul Reviving Wine
description: This Soul Reviving Wine in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book III, prepared for the Lord's Supper, hymn 17, headed “Incomparable food; or, The flesh and blood of Christ”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: This soul re-viv-ing wine, Dear Sa-viour, 'tis thy blood; We thank that sa-cred flesh of thine For this im-mor-tal food.

lines: We thank that sacred flesh of thine
Earth hath no dainties half so sweet
For there was no such blessed fruit
They feast upon their Maker's love,
And meets us with some cheering word,
This wine will drown your sad complaints,
And tune your voice to sing.
Thro' the wide earth his grace proclaim

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
